guides.title: Controlled server DataTable
guides.summary: Render a server page with typed columns, stable selection and native keyboard controls.
guides.markdown:
Import DataTable, DataTableProps<Row>, DataTableColumn<Row> and DataTableState from the public UI package. Compose with component(DataTable<Row>, props). Columns use either a key from the row type or an accessor function. An optional cell callback receives the typed row and returns a renderer value. Without a cell callback, values render as escaped text.

Provide rows for the current page, rowCount for all matching records, and a one-based state containing page, pageSize, filter and optional sort. The table does not fetch, sort, filter or slice data. onStateChange receives a new query state. Filtering, sorting and page-size changes reset page to 1. The parent must fetch that state and prevent stale responses from replacing newer results. Reconcile a page beyond the updated total in the parent. The Previous page control can recover to the new last page.

getRowId must return a stable, nonempty string. Duplicate row and column IDs are rejected. Never derive an ID from the page index. For selection, provide both selection and onSelectionChange. The callback receives a fresh Set. Select-visible affects only selectable rows on this page and preserves off-page IDs. Filtering preserves IDs too. Clear or reconcile selection in the parent when your application policy requires it. Always authorize selected IDs on the server before an action.

Use loading while a query is pending, error for a safe user-facing failure message, and onRetry for retry behavior. Stale rows can remain visible while loading, but selection is blocked. Empty results and an empty out-of-range page have separate status text. The table forwards no arbitrary HTML attributes. Use its declared props rather than relying on an untyped attribute spread.

A visible caption is required. Give each table a unique id when query changes use same-page navigation. It supplies stable IDs for the filter, page-size, sort and paging controls so Cossack can restore focus after replacing the page. Native table headers, buttons, search input, select and checkboxes provide semantics and keyboard behavior. rowLabel names each selection checkbox and defaults to its ID. Sort headers expose aria-sort. The page-selection checkbox reports a mixed state. Paging buttons remain focusable with aria-disabled and ignore inactive actions, preserving focus during loading and at page boundaries. Retry moves focus to the filter before invoking the callback. Loading and result counts use a polite status region; errors use an alert. Load the UI theme as for other UI components.

The public-type, SSR and Chromium HTTP-data tests cover this contract. Generated Node and local workerd applications exercise server resources, URL queries, selection and hydration. The full runtime matrix and broader UI accessibility audit remain separate acceptance work.

guides.title: Typed native controls
guides.summary: Use native attributes, @event listeners and accessible labels with Button, Input, Label, Checkbox, Switch and Form.
guides.markdown:
Button, Input, Label, Checkbox, Switch and Form declare native attributes without an arbitrary string/any index signature. component() checks the component's own props. Pass children as its third argument. Use lower-case HTML attribute names, such as tabindex and readonly. Native disabled/required values are booleans, not strings or loading counts. Use !!loading or loading > 0. Visual size is default, sm or lg; it is not the numeric HTML input size. data-* accepts scalar values. ARIA attributes use DOM-defined names and serialize booleans/numbers as text.

Use @click, @input, @change and other DOM event names. React-style onClick is not a listener. NativeEvents<Element> gives each listener the DOM event type and the exact control as currentTarget. target can be a descendant. Capture currentTarget before awaiting; native events clear currentTarget after dispatch. Form's submit callback has an HTMLFormElement currentTarget and prevents native navigation. It defaults to novalidate; set novalidate:false to keep browser constraint validation. Omit submit for a native form submission. Choose Button type explicitly inside forms: button for actions, submit for submission, reset for native reset behavior. A missing type retains the browser's submit default.

Input's value attribute supplies native default markup. Use .value for reactive values, bind() for two-way binding or live() for explicit DOM reconciliation. The .checked and .indeterminate properties are also available on Input. Checkbox and Switch instead own checked through their checked prop; use @change and event.currentTarget.checked to update parent state. Do not override their type, role or checked property through a competing spread. Checkbox supports indeterminate and label; label takes precedence over children. Switch children supply visible label content. Native form names and values are forwarded to the input, so unchecked/disabled controls follow normal FormData rules.

Give Input a visible Label with matching for/id, or an aria-label. Checkbox and Switch need label content or aria-label. Icon-only buttons need an accessible name. Link field help/errors with aria-describedby and publish validation state with aria-invalid. Labels, keyboard behavior and native disabled/required validation remain browser-owned. class merges with the component's base classes; id, names, ARIA, data attributes and listeners target the native control, not the Checkbox/Switch label wrapper.

Published declaration tests reject misspelled props/events, invalid values and competing control ownership. Chromium covers labels, keyboard toggles, parent-controlled reset, native validation, event targets and FormData. Other UI components still have separate contract/accessibility audit work; this guide does not assert coverage for the entire catalog.

guides.title: Radio groups and numeric sliders
guides.summary: Keep native choice, range, form, event and accessibility behavior explicit.
guides.markdown:
RadioGroup renders a div with role=radiogroup and native radio inputs. Give each logical group a distinct nonempty name within its form, unique string item values, and an accessible group name through aria-label or aria-labelledby. Item labels fall back to their values. Optional item IDs must be unique in the document. Items are keyed by value so reordering retains their DOM identity. value identifies the current selection. Update it in onValueChange(value, event); event.currentTarget is the input. Native @change still bubbles to the root div, so that listener's currentTarget is HTMLDivElement and target is the input. Capture a native event's currentTarget before awaiting.

RadioGroup disabled, required and form apply to every input. Item disabled adds a per-choice restriction. Browser radio grouping, arrow keys and form validation remain native. orientation controls layout and aria-orientation. Other declared global attributes/events target the div, not each input. Text-input attributes and competing role/orientation overrides are rejected by types. Duplicate values and an empty name fail explicitly.

Slider renders a native range input. value, min, max and step are finite numbers; max must be at least min and step must be positive. The browser clamps the requested value and applies step. The component sets constraints before the controlled value and reconciles that value when bounds change, including when a previously clamped value becomes valid. Handle @input on the native input and read event.currentTarget.valueAsNumber to update parent state. Use Input with type=range if you need a direct native wrapper instead of this controlled Slider contract.

Give Slider a visible external Label using for/id, label, aria-label or aria-labelledby. label takes precedence over aria-label without emitting duplicate attributes. name, form and list target the input. The range type, numeric state and implicit value semantics remain component-owned; text-input attributes and competing .value bindings are rejected. Disabled appearance follows native :disabled state, including inherited fieldsets.

Checkbox, Switch and RadioGroup labels style themselves from their child input's actual disabled state. This also handles inherited disabled fieldsets. Chromium acceptance builds the real Tailwind/UI theme and verifies light/dark disabled appearance, native keyboard behavior, a Switch focus ring, callback targets, parent radio resets, keyed identity and range bounds. This does not close the full UI catalog or runtime matrix.
